Security verdict: PASS

PR #291, exact head 46ee6d5c27ad3e2a1f6e0f148e9ed563c25d6a3a, base 74d1c63a97551b5ce18768db64a6bfa33cd97ee7. Reviewed the five-file F239/R288-FU-01 diff and the direct build-report producer/render boundary. No reportable security vulnerability found; no product files changed.

Evidence:
- crates/daemon/src/pa_watchdog.rs:1379-1403,1418-1450 rejects oversized reports and malformed trees. Commit prefixes accept hexadecimal identifiers with an optional +dirty suffix; source hashes accept hash: followed by hexadecimal digits. Malformed prefixes disclose only their byte count, not the supplied text.
- Interpolated tree identifiers are reconstructed by reported_tree from one to four lowercase hexadecimal components joined with +, not copied as arbitrary seat text. See pa_watchdog.rs:1362-1363,1383,1430-1435.
- pa_watchdog_tests.rs:1910-1935,1986-2016,2070-2110 covers instruction text, newlines, delimiter spoofing, ESC, BEL and NUL, including absence of hostile text/control characters from the digest.
- The daemon commit is its trusted compile-time Services::build_commit, also returned by ping: crates/daemon/src/lib.rs:78,699; crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:904. harness/scripts/release-build.sh:74-84 derives the stamp from git.
- All 12 added documentation lines were inspected and scanned for credential literals, home/private paths and private repository references; zero indicator matches. docs/difficulties.md:205 and docs/retros/pr288-review.md:1-11 contain no secrets, prohibited paths, private identities or private transcript content.

Trust scope: community/RULINGS.md:25,36-37 in the authoritative government root supplies C21/C32/C33. Closed grammars and safe rendering remain intact. Known C33 limit: build identities are self-reported, not attested; a trusted same-user caller can claim a matching tree and suppress the stale-extension diagnostic. This is not a new per-seat security boundary or a blocking finding.
